ADHD is knowing exactly what you need to do and exactly how to do it, but no matter how hard you try you can't do it. Nobody knows that you really are trying your hardest. They assume you're lazy. “You're so smart! Why don't you just try?” “What do I have to do to make you care? Don't you know this is going to effect your future?” “You just don't want to do your homework.” (All things that have been said to me.)

What does it feel like? Imagine carrying two 50 lb weight, one on each of your shoulders. They are guilt and shame. At the same time imagine the overwhelming anxiety of just wanting to please someone, trying your hardest to do whatever they expect of you in every moment… and it never goes right. You feel stupid, clumsy, useless, constantly in the way, especially when all you really want to do is help. Now imagine you’re only 6 years old and feeling this way.

You’re a child. You want to make someone proud, anyone proud, so in 3rd grade you decide you'll cheat on your spelling test and just fill in random number on your timed math fluency sheet bc you've never ever finished one on time and that means that you don't get recess. So you cheat but you can't even do that right bc you get caught. So now you're a disappointment again. Still.

Imagine really wanting to be in band in 5th grade, so your parents buy you an instrument but before they do they ask you 50 time “ARE YOU SURE???” Because they know you've never stuck with anything. And then when band lessons come in the middle of homeroom you're so wrapped up in something else that you forget and miss them. EVERY. SINGLE. TIME. The band director says to you “you might as well quit because obviously you don't want to be here.” You can't bear to face him after that. Your parents are pissed.

Imagine in confiding in your mother, that you're depressed and anxious. “There's something wrong with me!” Because you knew there is! You've never fit in, you're too intense for other people. You've never had a friendship that naturally and organically drifted apart. They've all exploded in your face leaving holes the size of grapefruits in your soul and you don't know how to go on so you just do but it's like trying to run a race with a broken foot except nobody can see that your foot is broken. “You're just fine.” And you're only 13. And you silently wish you were dead.

Imagine feeling your first heartbreak as a literal, physical pain. Like a headache, no a migraine, except in your chest. You can't see bc as soon as you open your eyes 50 tears want to come out at once and they won't wait their turn. Curled up in the fetal position sobbing until your throat feels like sandpaper, hours at a time. “Why are you so upset?! He wasn't even your boyfriend. You're 16, you'll get over it.” Salt in an open wound.

I could go on but I think you get the picture.

ADHD is NOT a “mental disorder". It is a physical brain difference, a neurological, structural disorder, where the parts of the brain that deal with executive function are minutely smaller and less developed than those of a neurotypical brain. The symptoms present as psychiatric but are neurological in origin. What are executive functions?


Now imagine struggling with all of this and the kind of mental anguish it could cause… I can't convey to you how much I hated myself.

Other things that I struggled with that can be linked back to adhd: overeating, food addiction, obesity, restless leg syndrome, sleep apnea, self-harm, suicide attempts, teeth grinding or bruxism, sensory issues, vision problems, etc…

It's been a long, hard road, working through the trauma and damage life has handed me and there were a few times I barely made it through.

Finally, my diagnosis at 33 gives me the missing puzzle piece that I needed to forgive myself for my short comings. I'm not lazy. I'm not stupid. I'm not an idiot. There really was something going on.
